note: Corrected per the lead's fourth review (F3): the v2 annotation still removed real wall as negative - source pixels (400,600) and (600,600) in frame 1 are wall but v2's foreground_occlusion table polygon (starting at (0,435)/(785,405)) covered them as a known negative, and the review named this a workflow problem, not a two-anchor problem. This version was built by a different workflow: (1) a labelled source-coordinate grid drawn directly onto each ORIGINAL 2560x1369 frame at native resolution before any resize (scripts in M4-F3-annotation-audit-2026-09-09/, all crops named with their own [x0,y0,x1,y1) source bounds - no resize ever precedes a grid draw, so no crop-origin/scale bug can enter silently); (2) forward-mapping verified at the image's own top-left and bottom-right corners (f1_corner_check.png, f1_corner_check_br.png) before tracing anything; (3) every wall/furniture boundary retraced from these grids by reading off real pixel transitions, at progressively finer grid spacing (50px down to 10px) around each boundary, NOT by adjusting vertices until a scorer accepted them - the anchors below were chosen by looking at the image first, then checked once against the composed masks as a bug check, the same order the review required. Frame 1's table polygon is now traced to its real corner (approx. (0,800)-(788,790)-(850,1040)-(862,1369)), which independently produces the review's own (400,600)/(600,600) as positive - not the other way around. Frame 2's furniture/bench boundary had the SAME class of bug (v1/v2 marked x:600-980,y:650-1369 negative, but the real wall/bench transition runs far lower, y:825-970 depending on x - found only because this audit re-traced every frame instead of the one named example). Frame 3's positive extent was previously cut off around y:600-750 even though the wall in this steep, close-up downward-pitched view genuinely fills the frame to y=1369 for x<1080 - re-traced and extended, with a genuinely ambiguous ceiling strip at the top (y<100 for x>650) now marked uncertain rather than silently included or excluded. uncertain_polygons remain genuinely ambiguous transitions excluded from scoring. wall_interior_anchors and negative_anchors are independently placed on both sides of each retraced boundary at several horizontal positions (not just the two the review cited) and checked by tests/test_boundary_scoring.py and scripts/verify_boundary_targets_v3.py against the composed masks - a check that the JSON encodes what the image trace found, not a re-decision of what the image shows. See M4-F3-annotation-audit-2026-09-09/ for the full contact sheet, corner-mapping checks, and this exact anchor table with reasons. v1 and v2 files are preserved untouched; this is a versioned annotation audit only - the proposal path never reads this file.
